title: Lease fencing and idempotent reset for reserved tenants
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Introduce a lease-fencing protocol and idempotent reset endpoint to ensure atomic, observable quota resets for reserved capacity tenants across regions and during clock skew or failover scenarios.
background: We have observed inconsistent quota reset behavior for reserved pools when regional failovers, clock skew, or duplicate reset attempts occur. Symptoms include double-counting of top-ups, transient over- or under-throttling, and billing reconcilers requiring manual corrections. Current reset is implemented as a best-effort per-region job without global fencing or idempotency keys.
goals: Guarantee at-most-once execution for monthly/daily/quasi-rolling reserved quota resets across replicas/regions
Provide lightweight fencing tokens so only the active controller may advance an epoch for a tenant
Expose an idempotent REST API for forced resets with auditable telemetry and safe rollback markers
Minimize added latency on normal quota checks and preserve existing SLOs
non_goals: Re-architecting the billing pipeline in this ticket; reconciliation tooling will be separate
Changing customer-visible quota semantics (no change to allowances or billing units)
design_decisions: Use a monotonic reset token (tenant-reset-seq) stored in centralized metadata (consistent store) and replicated to region-local caches
Make reset operation conditional on Compare-And-Swap on tenant-reset-seq to ensure atomic advancement
Introduce a short-lived controller lease (fencing token) to be acquired before any reset to prevent split-brain resets from multiple controllers
Provide an idempotency key in the reset API; if the key has been seen, return previous reset result instead of reapplying
Record a reset audit entry (immutable) containing controller-id, seq-before, seq-after, idempotency-key, and telemetry snapshot for debugging and billing audits
tradeoffs_and_risks: Centralized metadata store adds an availability dependency; mitigate with multi-region read-replicas and local fallback reads for reads-only paths
CAS updates can increase latency for rare concurrent reset attempts; acceptable since resets are infrequent (daily/monthly) and we keep critical path optimizations for steady-state token checks
Controller lease expiration under heavy GC or pause could lead to delayed resets; we will tune lease TTLs and add clock-skew tolerant checks
implementation_plan: 1) Add tenant-reset-seq column to metadata store with migration script (non-blocking backfill).
2) Implement fencing service: acquireLease(controller-id, tenant-id) -> fencing-token. Lease persisted with expiry and quorum-aware writes.
3) Extend reset API: POST /v2/tenants/:id/quota_reset { idempotency_key, target_window } — API performs AcquireLease -> CAS(seq) -> write audit log and emits telemetry.
4) Add local cache layer to read tenant-reset-seq for quota checks; invalidate on reset via pub/sub notification.
5) Backfill consumers: update quota microservices to consult tenant-reset-seq and short-circuit stale local resets.
6) Add migration-runbook and automated smoke tests exercising failover, duplicate resets, and clock skew scenarios.
7) Security review and key rotation for controller identities and audit log integrity checks.
8) Ship feature behind feature-flag and enable for internal accounts, then gradual rollout to reserved tenants.
9) Post-rollout: run reconciliation job to verify no double top-ups; manual remediation playbook if anomalies detected.
rollout_plan: Internal dogfood on staging for one week with duplicate-reset FTE tests
Enable for 5 pilot reserved tenants with low cross-region churn
Monitor for 48h, then expand to medium-size tenants, finally opt-in all reserved accounts
Keep legacy reset job disabled only after 1 week of zero anomalies and reconciliation confirmation
acceptance_criteria: Resets are idempotent: repeated POST with same idempotency_key returns identical audit id and does not reapply top-up
No double top-ups observed in pilot tenants during simulated controller failover tests
Audit logs for resets are immutable and include controller id and seq-before/after
Quota check latency p50 increase < 1ms and p99 increase < 6ms in steady-state
Automated reconciliation confirms zero net accounting divergence after 3 pilot reset cycles
monitoring_and_alerting: Dashboard: recent resets with seq-before/after, controller-id, region
qa_checks: Integration test: simultaneous reset attempts from two controllers must result in one success and one 409-like response
Chaos test: kill controller during reset and assert eventual consistency and no double top-up
Clock skew test: simulate +2m to -5m skew across regions and validate fencing still prevents double resets
Smoke test: idempotency key replay returns cached result and does not change balances
post_mortem_and_runbook: If double-top-up detected: use audit log to identify offending resets, reverse recent top-up and notify billing + customer success
If metadata store becomes unavailable: enter limited mode where resets are queued and alerts are triggered; notify SRE
If idempotency-store corrupt: fallback to manual reconciliation and enable read-only mode for billing until fixed
